definition: her best-behaviour script coming down while my own reach thins

settled:
The difficulty between me and a typical person is mutual rather than one-sided, and on my side it is also uneven: strong early, weak deep.

Milton's double empathy is the name for the mutual half. What I am adding is the mechanism: my modelling of them fails outbound and their modelling of me fails inbound, so the channel loses signal at both ends at once.

I rate my own first-contact skill at least as important as how well the other person can read me and adapt. The usual telling weights their side. I weight mine equally.

Two things fall at once as a relationship deepens, and they compound. Their best-behaviour script comes down as they get comfortable, and that script was a second safety contribution beyond my own skill. My own reach thins with closeness, whatever their script is doing.

The safe middle is safe because both are still near full strength: their script still up, my reach not yet thinned.

title: The Two Curves That Fall Together
